gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the four D cells' storage and cycle claims on the same terms. Done that way, Tenergy's 10,000 mAh D page makes no self-discharge claim at all, so it is not shown to be a low-self-discharge cell. EBL's own store gives its 10,000 mAh D cell 1,200 cycles on one page but says C and D cells get 'up to 500 charge cycles' on another, where only AA and AAA carry the 80%-after-3-years claim. Powerex is the only maker that states a minimum capacity (9,000 mAh).
standout_why: I compared against newworldsurvival.com (cited in chat 2), reactual.com (cited in both chats) and the Powerex MH-DP100 sheet (cited in both chats). New World Survival lists Centura at 2,100 cycles and 85% after 1 year, and EBL at 1,200 cycles and 80% after 3 years. It gives no test conditions, does not cover Tenergy's 10,000 mAh D cell, and does not mention EBL's own 500-cycle C/D figure. Reactual names Powerex and Tenergy at 10,000 mAh but gives no retention figure for any named product and no cycle life. Only the Powerex sheet has a minimum capacity, and it covers one product. None of them puts the four claims side by side, and none notes that Tenergy's 10,000 mAh D page has no retention claim.
decides: This confirms Tenergy Centura (85% after 1 year, 2,100 cycles) or Powerex Precharged (85% after 1 year, 9,000 mAh minimum) for emergency or stored use. It weakens ChatGPT's 'Tenergy Premium 10,000 mAh for frequent use' pick for anyone who stores cells, because Tenergy states no retention for it. It also undercuts EBL's 1,200-cycle 'value' case, since EBL itself also says 500 for D cells. For storage, the rated mAh matters less than whether the maker states a retention figure.
